preferences.startingPriorityHint: Passes whenever you have nothing meaningful to do, and stops when you can respond.
preferences.startingPriorityStopsHint: Also stops on every opponent spell and ability, and on combat damage — even when you can't respond.
preferences.startingPriorityFullHint: Never passes for you: you get every priority window.
preferences.forcedInstantHint: When a question has only one legal answer, the game answers it at once and shows a notice.
preferences.forcedDelayedHint: The game answers a question with only one legal answer after a short pause, and shows a notice.
preferences.forcedAskHint: Every question waits for you, even one with a single legal answer.
preferences.lockedPriority: You always get priority in your own main phases
preferences.startingPriorityNote: Every game starts in this mode. The mode button next to Pass still switches it for the game you're in.
preferences.alwaysStopHint: Extra stops on top of the automatic ones — the engine holds priority here even when you have nothing to do. Clicking a step in the in-game step strip changes the same list.
preferences.stopAtOnOpponentTurn: Stop at {{step}} on an opponent's turn
preferences.holdPriorityHint: Normally your own spells and abilities pass straight to your opponent. Switch a kind on to get priority back while it waits on the stack — only when you have something you can cast or activate in response.
preferences.myTriggeredAbilitiesHint: Respond to your own trigger before it resolves — for example, shrink the creature targeted by a pending Jaws of Defeat trigger.
preferences.myActivatedAbilitiesHint: Respond to an ability you just activated, for example by activating another one on top of it.
preferences.mySpellsHint: Respond to a spell you just cast, for example to copy it or to put another spell above it on the stack.
preferences.autoTapHint: Pay costs automatically when you cast a spell or activate an ability. Turn this off to choose the mana sources yourself.
preferences.autoOrderTriggersHint: When several of your abilities trigger at once, they go on the stack in the order they triggered — except an ability checking something that happened this turn resolves after the rest. Turn this off to choose the order whenever it can matter, such as scrying before drawing or creating a token before adding counters. In Full Control you always choose.
preferences.followActionHint: In games with three or more players, move the camera to the board where something is happening.
preferences.battlefieldDescription: Identical permanents — same name, tapped state, counters, damage and so on — can collapse into a stack.
preferences.landExamples: Basic lands, dual lands, and more
preferences.visibleStackLayersHint: How many cards a stack fans out before the rest hide behind its count badge. Fewer layers save room on crowded boards.
preferences.reduceMotionHint: Cut animations and transitions short. “Follow system” uses your device's accessibility setting.
preferences.cardPreviewHint: Show the large card image when the mouse rests on a card. Touch screens keep their long-press preview.
preferences.messageAlertsHint: In a game, a draft or the deckbuilder, show an unread count on the chat button and preview new messages. When off, they wait quietly until you're back on the home screen.
preferences.preferencesButtonTitle: Preferences — priority stops, card stacking, and motion
